bugs.description: hd-pow computes pv2 (expt bv (- n 2)) unconditionally. For n=1, this results in expt bv -1, causing a division by zero or crash when the base is 0. This occurs even though the second derivative of f(x)=x is mathematically zero and should be stable.
bugs.fix_suggestion: Special-case n=1 and n=2 in hd-pow to avoid negative exponents, or check if the base is zero and handle the derivatives accordingly.

bugs.description: dual-pow (forward mode) crashes for exponents n < 1 at base 0 due to negative power in the derivative. While the derivative is infinite, a crash prevents the system from returning +inf.0/NaN or handling it gracefully in an optimization loop.
bugs.fix_suggestion: Guard the expt call in the derivative term to return infinity when the base is zero and n < 1.

bugs.description: traced-pow (reverse mode) suffers from the same zero-base crash as dual-pow for n < 1.
bugs.fix_suggestion: Add a check for (and (zero? bv) (< n 1)) in traced-pow and provide a safe local gradient (e.g., infinity).

bugs.description: Operations like dual-div, dual-recip, hd-div, and dual-log lack guards against division by zero or log of non-positive numbers. This relies on the underlying Scheme implementation's handling of division by zero, which often results in a crash rather than a numeric infinity.
bugs.fix_suggestion: Implement a safe-div helper or add explicit guards to return +inf.0 when the denominator is zero.

bugs.description: Inverse trigonometric functions (dual-asin, dual-acos) and their hyperdual/traced counterparts crash at the boundaries x = 1 or x = -1 because the derivative 1/sqrt(1-x^2) involves division by zero.
bugs.fix_suggestion: Guard the denominator in asin/acos gradients to handle the singularity at the boundaries.

bugs.description: The *current-tape* parameter is defined and managed within scopes but is never utilized as a default by traced-op. This makes the parameterization logic redundant as the tape is currently always extracted explicitly from traced arguments.
bugs.fix_suggestion: Either utilize (*current-tape*) as a fallback in traced-op or remove the unused parameter to simplify the AD scope logic.

bugs.description: reset-traced-ids! is deprecated and dangerous for nested AD as it resets the global counter without scope protection. It prints a warning but remains accessible.
bugs.fix_suggestion: Remove the deprecated function or make it private, ensuring all internal tests and examples have migrated to with-fresh-ad-scope.
